title: Prompt & Telemetry Retention Rules Builder and Legal‑Ready Evidence Packager
creator: Avery Chen
description: Build a first-class, declarative Retention Rules Builder focused on prompts, responses, request logs, and derived metrics. The builder will produce machine-readable policies that drive enforcement (HSM/KMS-backed purges, sampled archival) and generate 'legal-ready' evidence packages (signed manifests + hashed artifacts) for audits and requests. This work spans UI/Console, public API / SDK, backend enforcement hooks, and evidence export orchestration.
goal: Enable customers and compliance teams to author per-tenant, per-route retention policies via a guided UI, preview the concrete effects (sampled artifacts and size/region impact), run dry-runs, and produce automated signed evidence bundles suitable for legal/regulatory review.
acceptance_criteria: Console: Retention Rules Builder UI that lets users create rules targeting: prompts, responses, request-logs, and metrics with TTL, sampling rate, and residency hints.
API: Public policy DSL endpoint that returns canonical enforcement plan for a given tenant and time window.
Dry-run: Preview mode that shows estimated counts, storage impact, and example artifacts that would be deleted/archived.
Evidence export: One-click export that packages artifacts with attestation (SHA256 manifest, signing by tenant key or Redwood KMS, tamper-evident index) and a human-readable audit report.
Enforcement: Backend enforcement ensures purge/archival actions are scheduled and logged; test harness demonstrates deletion and archival flows in staging.
Cross-region: Rules respect data-residency hints; evidence exports include region provenance.
Security: Security review completed and threat-model mitigations implemented for export transport and key-handling.
Docs: PRD + Console help snips + API spec published in Confluence and SDK samples checked into SDK repo.
E2E tests: Automated tests that simulate TTL expiration, dry-run validation, and evidence export verification.
implementation_notes: Use existing retention orchestration (ENG-22456) as the enforcement engine; implement a policy translation layer that consumes DSL and emits scheduled purge/archive jobs.
Evidence packaging: follow hashed manifest format used by PM-21234 but extend with tenant-signed attestation and region metadata.
Console: Builder should be wizard-first (preset templates for common compliance regimes: GDPR, CCPA, FINRA) and an advanced editor exposing the policy DSL.
Dry-run engine will sample real indexes to estimate counts; sampling rate surfaced in preview and affects confidence intervals in estimates.
Respect per-route overrides and inheritance: route-level TTLs override tenant defaults and can be forced-only with org-admin permission.
Retention windows must be enforced consistently across hosted, dedicated, and private deployments; for Private, builder will emit a downloadable policy bundle and validation checks.
Telemetry: instrument policy evaluation time, purge job durations, archived artifact counts, and evidence bundle generation latency for the console dashboard.
UX: provide a timeline view showing how a request lifecycle maps to retention rules (ingest -> TTL -> archive/purge -> evidence snapshot).
decision_log: 2025-02-14: Chose a hybrid approach — declarative DSL + visual builder. Reason: developers need both machine-readability for enforcement and a UX for compliance teams.

2025-02-20: Evidence export format will use SHA256 manifests and support tenant-managed keys (preferred) with fallback to Redwood signing. Reason: legal teams prefer tenant signatures, but some customers cannot manage keys.

2025-02-27: Dry-run will be estimation-first (sampled) rather than deterministic to avoid large scans; accuracy metadata will be shown. Trade-off: speed vs exactness; mitigated by allowing on-demand full-scan for compliance investigations.
2025-03-01: Cross-region residency will be advisory in UI when Private deployment cannot enforce region affinity; backend will tag evidence with region-of-origin regardless.

risk_and_mitigation: Risk: Dry-run estimates may undercount for cold partitions. Mitigation: show confidence interval and allow ad-hoc full-scan exports for audits.
Risk: Evidence bundles could expose sensitive PII. Mitigation: default anonymization presets and PII redaction pipeline with customer override only via org-admin and audit logging.
Risk: Tenant key mismanagement. Mitigation: provide hosted KMS fallback and automated rotation hints; require explicit consent to use tenant keys for signing.
Risk: Cross-region enforcement limits in Private deployments. Mitigation: clearly surface advisory warnings and include region provenance in exported manifests.

Regression: ensure existing retention features (ENG-22456) unaffected; smoke tests for other console flows.
Security validation: key handling, bundle signing, transport encryption, and permission checks.
